channel.title: Cadence Evidence — PT Research Signal
channel.description: Daily curated physical therapy & rehab research for clinicians. AI-scored signal from 56 sources.

item.title: Rehabilitation of Athletes With Hamstring Strain Injury: SONAFE-Brazil Clinical Practice Guideline.
item.description: The National Society of Sports Physical Therapy (SONAFE-Brazil) has published a clinical practice guideline using the GRADE approach for rehabilitating athletes with hamstring strain injury, providing evidence-based guidance for physical therapists.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Structured exercise interventions and survival outcomes in patients with cancer: systematic review and meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 21 RCTs (n=3828 for OS) found structured exercise associated with significant improvements in overall survival (HR 0.77, 95% CI 0.65-0.92), disease-free survival (HR 0.83, 95% CI 0.72-0.95), all-cause mortality (RR 0.82, 95% CI 0.70-0.97), and cancer-specific mortality (RR 0.74, 95% CI 0.57-0.96). Evidence certainty was moderate for key outcomes.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Optimal exercise dose in adults with chronic low back pain disorders: systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review with dose-response network meta-analysis of 239 trials found that low-to-moderate exercise doses were associated with short-term clinically meaningful improvements in disability and pain intensity for chronic low back pain, with limited additional benefit at higher exposure. Optimal doses were predicted as 4 sessions/week, 25 min/session over 13 weeks for disability, and 3 sessions/week, 30 min/session over 8 weeks for pain.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Is Reduced Spinal Range of Motion a Prognostic Factor for Pain Intensity, Disability, and Global Recovery in People With Specific or Nonspecific Spinal Pain? A Systematic Review.
item.description: A systematic review of 37 studies found very low certainty evidence on whether reduced spinal range of motion is a prognostic factor for pain intensity, disability, and global recovery in people with specific or nonspecific spinal pain, with most studies reporting no clear association and high risk of bias.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Exercise-only interventions and exercise-based multidomain lifestyle interventions to promote cognitive function in older adults without dementia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 227 studies found that exercise-only interventions significantly improved executive functions, memory, and processing speed in older adults without dementia compared to control; exercise-plus interventions were significantly better than exercise-only for executive functions and processing speed.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Mirror therapy versus functional electrical stimulation cycling in post-stroke lower limb rehabilitation: a randomized controlled trial.
item.description: A randomized controlled trial (n=45) found that both mirror therapy (MD -2.60, 95% CI -5.83 to -0.63, p=0.004) and functional electrical stimulation-assisted cycling (MD -3.00, 95% CI -6.23 to -0.23, p=0.008) improved lower extremity motor function more than conventional rehabilitation in subacute stroke patients, with no significant difference between the two adjunct therapies.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Shear wave elastography for assessing lower extremity muscle stiffness after anterior cruciate ligament reconstruction: A systematic review.
item.description: A systematic review of six studies (173 ACLR participants, 79 controls) found shear wave elastography (SWE) detects muscle-specific mechanical deficits after ACLR, with reduced passive vastus medialis shear modulus (g -1.10 to -1.21) and semitendinosus stiffness (g -1.29 to -1.64) after hamstring harvest.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: A Return to Performance Continuum for Football (Soccer) Players After ACL Reconstruction: Bridging Rehabilitation, Return to Play and Sustained Performance.
item.description: This paper outlines a staged return-to-performance continuum for football players after ACL reconstruction, comprising structured on-field rehabilitation, return to team training, return to competitive match play, and sustained performance, underpinned by four interdependent pillars: movement quality, technical/tactical re-training, physical reconditioning, and neuromuscular performance restoration.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Effects of TENS, NMES, and Combination Therapy on Hemiplegic Shoulder Pain and Function After Stroke.
item.description: A 3-week RCT (N=60) found that combined TENS and NMES significantly reduced hemiplegic shoulder pain (VAS) and SPADI scores compared to TENS alone in acute and subacute stroke patients. All groups improved across multiple outcomes, but the combined therapy did not significantly improve upper extremity motor function, spasticity, or ADLs beyond individual therapies.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Prehabilitative Exercise Mitigates Immobilization-Induced Atrophy Through Muscle Reserve Rather Than Resistance to Disuse: The PRE-EX Randomized Controlled Trial
item.description: The PRE-EX trial (n=54) demonstrated that prehabilitative exercise mitigated immobilization-induced atrophy by increasing quadriceps CSA by 6.7% and MVC by 15.2% before disuse, rather than by altering the muscle's physiological response to immobilization.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Comparative effectiveness of digital health interventions for low back pain: systematic review and network meta-analysis of randomised controlled trials
item.description: A network meta-analysis of 84 RCTs (n=11,649) found that virtual reality (VR) showed the largest estimated post-intervention effects versus control for low back pain intensity (SMD -1.43, 95% CI -1.87 to -0.98), physical function, pain-related fear avoidance, and health-related quality of life.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Effects of Somatosensory Interventions on Sensory, Motor, and Balance Functions in Individuals with Stroke: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of nine RCTs (N=330) found that somatosensory interventions significantly improved Berg Balance Scale scores in stroke patients compared to conventional therapy, though no significant effects were observed for upper limb motor function.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Percutaneous Electrolysis for the Management of Musculoskeletal Disorders. A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis found very low-certainty evidence that adding percutaneous electrolysis (PNE) to therapeutic exercise was not superior to sham or exercise alone for pain or function in tendinopathies. Low-certainty evidence suggested PNE plus exercise might reduce short-to-medium term pain more than dry needling plus exercise in tendinopathy but not in myofascial pain syndrome.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Do blood flow restriction exercises offer additional benefits when compared to conventional exercises in musculoskeletal rehabilitation? A systematic review and meta-analysis
item.description: This systematic review and meta-analysis of 45 RCTs (n=1652) found low-certainty evidence that low-load exercise with blood flow restriction (LLE-BFR) was superior to low-load exercise (LLE) for muscle strength (SMD=0.82) and disability (SMD=0.63). Moderate-certainty evidence showed no clear difference between LLE-BFR and high-load exercise (HLE) for muscle strength (SMD=0.08). Pain reductions for LLE-BFR were small and not clinically meaningful.
item.author: BJSM

item.title: Calf Injuries: An Anatomy-Based Approach to Diagnosis, Management and Return to Sport.
item.description: A review of calf muscle injuries highlights the heterogeneity of lesions and emphasizes an anatomy-based approach to diagnosis and management, moving beyond muscle-based classifications. It supports criteria-based, progressive loading rehabilitation and multifactorial return-to-sport decisions, noting limited evidence linking specific anatomical patterns to prognosis.
item.author: PubMed

item.title: An exploration of self-evaluation of induced temporal and spatial gait asymmetry in neurotypical young adults.
item.description: A study in 33 neurotypical adults found that self-evaluation of temporal gait asymmetry was more accurate than spatial asymmetry (OR = 0.09 [0.02, 0.51] for presence) and directing attention to the swing phase improved temporal asymmetry self-evaluation (OR = 0.13 [0.04, 0.40]).
item.author: PubMed

item.title: Applications of MyotonPRO in the upper limb: a scoping review of orthopaedic, traumatologic, rehabilitation, and sports medicine evidence
item.description: A scoping review of 243 studies found MyotonPRO promising for assessing upper limb soft tissue biomechanical properties and monitoring exercise effects, but highlighted significant methodological heterogeneity and small sample sizes, particularly in orthopedic and traumatology fields.
item.author: BMC Musculoskelet Disord

item.title: Target Precision Shapes Trunk Compensation After Stroke: Neuromechanical Consequences for Upper Limb Rehabilitation
item.description: In individuals with stroke, trunk compensation was 15% lower for large targets than small targets, independently of arm weight. Movement time was 24% longer for small targets. This suggests trunk compensation is modulated by task demands, indicating that rehabilitation should evaluate compensation by its functional role and treat target size as an adjustable parameter.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Beyond Walking Speed: Estimating and Classifying Post-Stroke Gait Propulsion From Standardized Clinical Measures
item.description: Standardized clinical measures (6MWT, SPPB, TUG, FMA-LE, chronicity) can estimate post-stroke gait propulsion metrics (paretic propulsion peak, impulse, interlimb symmetry) with R² up to 0.81 and classify propulsion impairment with 84.8% accuracy. This offers a practical assessment in settings without specialized instrumentation.
item.author: medRxiv

item.title: Dextrose prolotherapy for chronic symptomatic rotator cuff tendinopathy and subacromial bursitis: A systematic review and meta-analysis.
item.description: A systematic review and meta-analysis of 14 studies (13 RCTs, 1 observational) found very uncertain evidence for dextrose prolotherapy for chronic symptomatic mixed rotator cuff tendinopathy and/or subacromial bursitis, showing little to no benefit compared to normal saline (SMD medium-term: -0.3 [-1.0; 0.4]; very low COE) and possibly worse physical performance compared to corticosteroid injections.
item.author: PubMed
